reliability_note: no published quota: the operator contacts a heavy user rather than throttling one, and the free network is one region with routing chosen by the visitor's ISP

evidence.proved: operator, 2026-05-28: a free user at 1-2 TB/day was tolerated, and regional bandwidth cost decides whether contact happens

notes: The strongest free relay found and the least durable evidence: two sentences, one operator, one day (2026-05-28). Stays reported. The same thread says the tolerance moves with regional bandwidth cost, so the number is a cost observation rather than a policy. Free includes a generic UDP entry and the game presets; SSH, HTTPs, TCP and TCP+UDP are Premium. Adds the date the tolerance was stated and the current free/Premium split read from the pricing page today. Re-read 2026-10-23: 'Minecraft Bedrock (NetherNet)' is now a premium-gated preset, so the free set is not every game preset. Custom UDP stays free.

extras.transit_note: the anycast relay carries the game traffic it forwards

binding_note: An unpublished tolerance is weaker than a quota because no threshold can be designed against, but this one is measured per day and generous: 1 TiB/month is 33.3 GiB/day, against a stated tolerance of about 1-2 TB/day for a single free user. What fails first is the free tier's protocol gate, not volume: generic TCP tunnels need Premium, so only the game presets and the generic UDP entry are available at zero cost.
interface_detail: the playit agent opens a tunnel to a global anycast address
